digest.component_or_area: rebar Jira Data Center reconciler live verification harness
propositions: The epic's headline AC (a DC-created issue appears locally after inbound, a local edit appears on DC after outbound) was not met because the live pass ran against an empty store, so convergence proved nothing.

Verification must run against a scrubbed, isolated copy of the real ticket store: a fresh git repo with no remote, REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=off, no Cloud credentials, and all .bridge_state* binding/snapshot artifacts removed and asserted absent.

Every DC-side mutation (14 inbound, 14 outbound) must round-trip and be asserted individually against a named oracle, except set_parent's epic case which asserts NotImplementedError directly against the transport; outbound update cells need a binding via the bound_dc_issue fixture.
--filter-local-ids failed to match inbound creates because it only matched local_id not the Jira key target, suppressing inbound apply; fixed by passing both identifiers.

Both directions are now proven live over the real store copy plus multi-page pagination, but the comprehensive mutation suite, per-mutation idempotence, positive inbound-identity assertion, and base_url file-content check remain open, so the story is not complete.

The snapshot differ (differ.py) is invoked with the previous remote snapshot as the local-source argument, emitting spurious inert outbound update/create echoes one pass after any write, producing unconvergeable churn and phantom probes for deletions — a product defect and sibling of a label-only fix.
